title: What If a Speck of Paint Hit the Space Station?

scenes.text: What if a speck of paint, far thinner than a hair, hit the space station?
Orbital debris can move at up to 17,500 miles an hour.
In 2016, something no more than a few thousandths of a millimeter wide struck a window in the Cupola.
It gouged a chip about seven millimeters wide out of the glass.
The window has four layers. The crew stayed safe and the station kept working.
A speck the size of dust, and a crater you can see from inside.

description:
What if a speck of paint hit the space station?
In 2016, debris no more than a few thousandths of a millimeter wide, probably paint or a metal flake, chipped a Cupola window on the International Space Station. The chip was about seven millimeters across and the crew was never in danger.
What should we run through next?
